evidenceHierarchy.title: Credit and the channel before the frameworks — Run 7's sequencing
evidenceHierarchy.note: For the second run running, credit and physical-channel signals arrived before the research frameworks, the same pattern as Run 6's AVGO CDS in August. Jupiter: Barclays flagged the air-permit and pipeline risk on 9 September, Oracle served force majeure on the 24th, and a lender sold the project debt below 90 cents on the 25th–26th. Kyber: a rack expert said the all-copper NVL144 was out of the 2027 plan on 9 September; UBS dated the slip to 2028 on the 13th and ISI wrote “Rubin/Kyber delays” on the 21st. CoreWeave: CDS widened 259bp to 811bp before UBS initiated at Buy and JPM upgraded. In each case the frameworks followed the price.
rungs: Physical-channel signals — permits, force-majeure notices, rack plans, delay trackers
Borrower-tier credit — neocloud CDS, project-debt marks, HY data-centre paper
Guarantor credit — NVDA CDS and the hyperscaler CDS average, which say whether distress is spreading up the chain
Equity research frameworks and targets, which followed the price in all three cases this run

call.headline: Own contracted, self-funded scarcity; underweight whatever must be refinanced or re-priced — and hedge with options, not bonds.
call.body: One stance, and a refinement of Run 6 rather than a reversal. Run 6's break condition — IG Tech tightening through 100bp while the tenant spread compresses — did not fire; the opposite happened. CoreWeave went to 811bp against ~88bp for hyperscalers, a ~720bp gap against Run 6's ~250bp watch level, so the discrimination paid. What the run added is a second axis cutting through the same names: whether today's price is contracted or has to be re-struck. CSPs agreed higher 1Q27 DRAM prices while September spot turned negative; B200 rents rose 50% while paid token prices fell 11–62%; seat software is being discounted 30–50% at the largest vendor; neoclouds are priced for scarcity but must refinance at 10–13% with their first 5-year contracts rolling in CY27. In every market value accrues to the side that has locked in the price, the volume or the funding.
call.notRecommended: This is not a call to cut gross AI exposure. Fundamentals strengthened again: aggregate US cloud backlog exceeds 100% of sales, 84% of semis guided above the Street, and the contracted tier of every bottleneck tightened. Cutting exposure would be trading the September tape rather than the evidence. Nor is it a call on the direction of rates — the options hedge exists precisely because the rate path is now a two-sided tail.

instructions.title: Own contracted, self-funded scarcity
instructions.body: NVDA and AVGO — net-cash or low-leverage self-funders with contracted 2027–28 revenue, Lipacis's low-P/E dispersion picks at ~19–20x NTM — with one qualification on NVDA: its credit is now priced for its guarantor role (~$170bn of contingent exposure, CDS +36bp QTD), so NVDA CDS is this leg's early warning. TSMC (N3 above 100% utilisation, 17x/12x 2027/28E against the SOX at 29x/20x). Contracted HBM and server memory through Samsung and SK hynix. The optical laser layer (LITE, COHR): InP sold out, prepaid to 2031, repriced +50–60%. Hold Micron as an exposure sized to its contracted half — it is the name where both clauses of the stance collide.

instructions.title: Underweight what must be refinanced or re-priced
instructions.body: Neoclouds (CRWV, NBIS, IREN, Nscale) — stated honestly, this runs against the majority of equity research this run and is justified only by the credit tape at 811bp; the flip test is the CY27 recontracting price and the direction of CRWV CDS. Lab-dependent, vendor-financed structures, with Oracle the clearest case. The un-contracted memory tier (spot and channel DRAM, consumer NAND) as an exposure, not a ticker list. Seat-priced application software facing agent-era discounting — but not the non-bypassable billing nodes (identity, observability, payment rails, EDA consumption), which belong on the long side.

instructions.title: Hedge with options, not duration
instructions.body: Run 6's long-duration hedge lost money: the 10-year went from ~4.8% to ~5.2% in the window and the stock–bond correlation turned positive at +28–60%. Bond CTAs sit at the 1st percentile and 100% short, so a bond rally from here works as a second long on AI equities, not as insurance. Use index or SOX downside, or payer structures on neocloud credit where available.

whatChanged.headline: Every macro bear trigger fired — and the AI complex made new highs anyway.
whatChanged.body: The Fed hiked unanimously with hawkish dots, the 10-year went through 5%, Brent through $100 and diesel set records — yet the Nasdaq-100 closed at a record on 21–22 September and the SOX is up ~79% YTD. The washout had already happened a week earlier and for a different reason: the 14 September “pace the frontier” episode took semis down 5.5% in a day, and within a week the same story was re-priced as “safety is additive compute.” Under that tape sit the run's two real findings: the credit discrimination Run 6 predicted is now visible and wide, and the AI price structure has split into inflating compute rents and deflating tokens.
whatChanged.stanceRefinement: The recommendation sharpens rather than reverses. “Contracted” joins “self-funded” as the sorting axis, and the hedge moves from duration to options because the stock–bond correlation turned positive and Run 6's long-duration hedge lost money.

bullets.title: Oil through $100, the war widens then half-reverses
bullets.body: Houthi attacks shut part of Saudi Arabia's southern facilities on 8 September; US forces sank five Iranian tankers on the 9th and Brent went through $100. Oil fell 3% on the 11th on a GCC–Iran meeting in Oman — the same day core CPI printed +0.3% m/m against +0.2% expected and US diesel crossed $6 for the first time.

bullets.title: Oracle: the cleanest demand proof and the cleanest financing warning
bullets.body: OCI +121%, RPO $664bn, and 100% of GPU capacity up for renewal renewed or resold at a 20% premium at 97.9% utilisation. But FCF was −$5.4bn, roughly −$16.8bn excluding $11.4bn of customer prepayments, with up to $20bn more FY27 financing under consideration and purchase obligations up 2.6x q/q to $34.2bn.

bullets.title: “Pace the frontier” — the flush and the six-day reversal
bullets.body: On 14 September semis fell 5.5%, optical 7%, memory 6% and TMT momentum 6% while yields rose 1–2bp — an intra-equity narrative re-pricing, not macro risk-off. By the 18th NSR's point (~80% of training compute already sits outside pre-training) and Jefferies' bus tour had turned safety into a compute-additive line.

bullets.title: The Warsh Fed's first hike
bullets.body: +25bp to 3.75–4.00%, unanimous (ISI had forecast a 10–2 split); median dot 4.1% for 2026 and 2027. Warsh named hyperscaler debt issuance as a driver of long yields. The Run 6 rate fracture resolved: GS and ISI's hike readings were right and TMTB's cut odds were the mis-specified side.

bullets.title: The credit tape discriminates, the equity tape ignores it
bullets.body: CoreWeave's 8-K showed ~$40m/MW short-dated contracts and +25% July pricing, and it launched a $3.0bn convertible and a 35m-share ATM the same day. By the 21st its CDS was 811bp (+259bp QTD) while the Nasdaq closed at a record and META rose 11% on Muse. The FT published OpenAI's −$278bn cumulative 2026–30 FCF plan.

bullets.title: The rates shock, force majeure and the memory turn
bullets.body: The 5-year closed above 5% for the first time since 2004 and Barr cited the AI investment surge; UBS went Underweight Tech in IG and HY. Oracle served force majeure on Jupiter (24th). Lipacis told ISI's whole client base semis are in the “late innings” (25th). Akamai signed an $11.6bn all-CPU contract with Anthropic, and Texas halted state data-center permits.

bullets.title: Credit and the channel led again
bullets.body: Jupiter, Kyber and CoreWeave each followed the same order: the physical or credit signal first, the research frameworks days later. Three houses were bullish on CoreWeave's equity (UBS initiated at Buy, JPM upgraded, ISI held Outperform) while its CDS was blowing out.

layers.title: Operational fundamentals
layers.summary: Demand intact, the constraint has become deliverability, and the price structure has split. Cloud TTM bookings hit $1.4tn (+191% y/y) and aggregate US cloud backlog now exceeds 100% of sales, up from ~50% last autumn. What binds is converting that demand into energised racks: GPUs are “Balanced” at 30–40 weeks while N3 runs at 106–113% utilisation, InP contract prices rose 50–60%, and UBS's first delay tracker shows 7.0GW of US capacity affected. The most important new fact: compute rents are inflating (B200 +50%) while token prices deflate (OpenAI −62%).

layers.title: Market structure
layers.summary: A narrative flush did the washout, and the complex re-levered into a rates shock. The 14 September pacing flush cleared positioning a week before the FOMC; post-FOMC selling lasted about 30 minutes; CTAs re-levered from the 13th to the 37th percentile. What makes the regime fragile: bonds no longer hedge (stock–bond correlation +28–60%), hedge-fund tech net leverage is at the 100th percentile, and only 49% of the S&P sits above its 200-day. Multiples are being cut while earnings rise — now written into the models.

layers.title: Financing and credit
layers.summary: Discrimination is confirmed, the borrower tier is priced as distressed, and the guarantor is now visible. CoreWeave CDS 811bp against a ~88bp hyperscaler average; Jupiter project debt sold below 90 cents; QTS −84bp against ZENARC +138bp. MS moved NVDA credit to Neutral on ~$170bn of off-balance-sheet exposure while keeping the equity at OW — “the same facts carry opposite signs by asset class.” Run 6's observable precursor fired, one rung down: at the neocloud tier rather than in IG Tech.

layers.title: Macro and policy
layers.summary: The gate resolved hawkish, and AI entered the Fed's reaction function by name. A unanimous hike, the 5-year above 5% for the first time since 2004, Brent +97.5% YTD, and refined products — not crude — as the binding inflation channel. Warsh and Barr both named AI financing and investment. UBS spells out the loop: hyperscaler capex adds to inflation, keeping the Fed hiking and term premium high, which raises the funding cost of the same capex. The policy surface also widened: Texas froze permits, a transceiver bill named InnoLight and Eoptolink, and the US–China truce was extended only to 10 January.

insights.headline: The AI price structure has split — compute rents inflate, tokens deflate
insights.claim: Value is flowing to whoever owns scarce, energised, contracted capacity and being squeezed out of the model layer and out of anything that must be refinanced.
insights.evidence: Ornn, June → September: B200 rents +50%, H200 +28%, and the B200 settlement index at $7.77/GPU-hr on 22 September. CoreWeave July prices +25% across SKUs with short-dated capacity at ~$40m/MW, about three times long-term rates. Against that, OpenAI's average paid token price fell 62%, DeepSeek 51%, Google 29% and Anthropic 11%; GPT-6 list prices −50% and Opus 5.5 ~−40% per workload. It explains the vertical-integration moves — Anthropic's 1GW Stream lease talks, the Akamai CPU contract, OpenAI's 8GW SB Energy lease. The counterweight: DeepSeek raised prices 2.3–4.5x without losing customers, so price cuts are a competitive choice rather than a cost floor.

priorRun.predicted: Not tracked — Run 6 carried GPU rents (#6) and enterprise token economics (#11) as separate rows and had no view on the spread between them.
priorRun.outcome: Added as indicator #32. The spread, not either level, now decides who captures value.

insights.headline: Credit discrimination is confirmed — the borrower tier is priced as distressed
insights.claim: The credit market charges by tenant quality, project stage and permitting, and the gap is now wide. Credit is not confirming a solvency problem in the AI winners; it is pricing distress in the borrower tier.
insights.evidence: CoreWeave 5Y CDS 811bp, +259bp QTD, notes T+530 → ~T+850, against a hyperscaler average of ~88bp (MSFT 44bp; ORCL 189bp the widest IG name). Jupiter project debt sold below 90 cents. QTS (IG, Blackstone) −84bp against ZENARC (HY) +138bp on a permit denial. US HY CCC at 923bp, the 100th percentile for 2026. Financing is constrained by price, not capacity: US IG tech issuance $321bn YTD against $113bn a year ago, books 3–5x covered.

priorRun.predicted: “The observable precursor is not a bankruptcy — it is spread widening in IG Tech while equities are still making highs.” Break condition: IG Tech tightening through 100bp while the tenant spread compresses.
priorRun.outcome: The break condition did not fire; the opposite happened. The divergence appeared one rung down — CoreWeave's CDS out 259bp in the quarter while the Nasdaq closed at records — a ~720bp tenant gap against the ~250bp watch level. IG Tech OAS itself had no print in this batch.

insights.headline: Equity research went long the name credit priced as distressed
insights.claim: Four equity houses turned or stayed bullish on neocloud scarcity pricing in the same week CoreWeave's CDS blew out. The upgrades are a bet that short-dated price inflation outruns the cost of the debt that funds it.
insights.evidence: UBS initiated CRWV at Buy $120, JPM upgraded to OW $125, ISI held OP $150, BNP upgraded NBIS to Outperform $399 (“The Price of Scarcity”); Rothschild initiated Sell on both and Bernstein holds Underperform $74. JPM's own model has CRWV FY28 net interest of $7.84bn against adjusted EBIT of $8.79bn and net debt rising to $115bn; ISI puts take-or-pay project ROIC at ~8–10%, close to a high-yield cost of debt. The equity case rests on years 7–10 of GPU life and CY27 recontracting at spot premia; credit prices recontracting into a world where token prices have halved.

priorRun.predicted: Neoclouds are “the AI that has to borrow” — underweight the balance-sheet-dependent tail.
priorRun.outcome: Not contradicted by the upgrades, but the stance now runs against the majority of equity research on the name and is justified only by the credit tape. Logged as a new two-asset-class dispute (⑩).

insights.headline: The guarantor is now visible in NVIDIA's own credit
insights.claim: Vendor financing is quantified on both sides, and the credit market is treating NVIDIA's guarantees as real exposure even though the equity multiple does not show it.
insights.evidence: MS models ~$200bn of NVIDIA all-in credit exposure by end-CY28, ~$170bn of it off funded debt (~$40bn lease adjustments, ~$65bn residual-value support, ~$65bn revenue-share floors, including a $2.12/hr GPU backstop floor), moved NVDA credit to Neutral while keeping the equity at OW, and notes DSO up from 45 to 60 days. NVDA 5Y CDS +36bp QTD. NSR counts >$1.4tn of NVIDIA- and Broadcom-architected facilities and ~$300bn of NVIDIA backstops against ~$260bn of annualised EBITDA. NVIDIA equity still trades at ~19x NTM.

priorRun.predicted: The market did not reprice NVIDIA's 52% cut to the OpenAI Ohio backstop — the cleanest live test, because the market was visibly not watching.
priorRun.outcome: Partially priced — through credit rather than equity. NVDA CDS +36bp QTD, a Neutral credit rating from MS, and the FT naming NVIDIA and Oracle as dependent on OpenAI's financing; the equity multiple still does not show it.

insights.headline: A narrative flush did the washout — before the macro gate could
insights.claim: Run 6 expected the macro gate to decide September. It did decide it, hawkishly, but by then the market had already de-grossed on a different story, and the complex was rebuilding exposure when the 5-year went through 5%.
insights.evidence: The 14 September pacing flush took semis −5.5%, optical −7%, neoclouds −7% and TMT momentum −6% with yields rising 1–2bp — a positioning event, not risk-off. UBS and Bernstein said no capex plan had changed. By 18 September safety had been re-priced as compute-additive; Ross later wrote that “Amodei marked the low day for Semis/AI.” Post-FOMC a −$62bn excess-sell burst lasted about 30 minutes; CTAs re-levered from the 13th to the 37th percentile.

priorRun.predicted: The September FOMC — one speech, four readings across three houses — would be the single largest source of near-term volatility and decide the month.
priorRun.outcome: The macro gate fired hawkishly, but the washout came a week earlier from the pacing narrative, and the tape made new highs through the macro triggers.

insights.headline: Bonds stopped hedging — the long-duration hedge lost money
insights.claim: With the stock–bond correlation positive and bond CTAs max short, a bond rally now works as a second long on AI equities rather than as insurance. The hedge has to be optionality.
insights.evidence: The 10-year went from ~4.8% to ~5.2% in the window; the stock–bond correlation is +28–60% (UBS desk). Bond CTAs sit at the 1st percentile over five years and 100% short USTs, LQD and HYG. ISI's CIO breakfast was unanimous that fixed income no longer hedges equities. A rally to a 4.80% 10-year would trigger short-covering that lifts equities too.

priorRun.predicted: Long duration is the corroborating hedge — bond CTAs at −1.00 with +$223bn of DV01-equivalent buying on a −52bp rally, so risk-off gets double amplification.
priorRun.outcome: Yields rose ~40bp through the window and the correlation turned positive; the hedge lost money. Indicator #17 marked Contradicted.

insights.headline: Earnings up, multiples down — now written into the models
insights.claim: Run 6's “targets cut on beats” regime generalised from semis to the whole AI complex, and rates rather than unit pricing are now the input most likely to move memory targets next.
insights.evidence: UBS held Micron at $1,625 while C2029 EPS rose from $165 to $219, cutting the multiple from 11x to 8x on a 5.00% 10-year in the cost of equity. MS cut AMAT from $642 to $563 and CAMT from $165 to $152 while raising EPS on both. Stifel upgraded MSFT while cutting FY28; Wells' +24% META target is all multiple; the KOSPI target was cut from 8,800 to 8,000 on rising EPS. 84% of semis guided above the Street, against 97% a quarter ago.

priorRun.predicted: Target prices are a corrupted signal — beat-and-raise with the target held or cut is the default expectation; read the EPS revision and the horizon, never the headline PT.
priorRun.outcome: Escalated and broadened: the multiple compression is now an explicit model input (a 5% 10-year in the cost of equity), across memory, semicap, software and platforms.

insights.headline: The memory top is resolved on mechanism — spot turned, the contracted tier firmed
insights.claim: The two sides of Run 6's top unresolved dispute describe different markets, and the equity market is paying for the allocated one. Timing is now dated by the sources themselves to 2Q–4Q27.
insights.evidence: ISI's September series: DDR5 16GB spot −1.8%, DDR4 16Gb −3.2%, NAND TLC −5.0%, and monthly DDR contract +18–19% in August → +2–3% in September; OEM inventory 70% above trend, early double-ordering. Raspberry Pi and Acer called the peak (grade c). Against that, CSPs agreed a higher 1Q27 DRAM ASP than 4Q26 (BofA), NAND contract guidance was raised to +21/+17/+15% q/q, and 2027 HBM contract prices are +80–100% (RBC). Citi has prices peaking 2Q27; UBS Gaudois has memory stocks peaking around 4CQ27.

priorRun.predicted: Hold the memory trim at the un-contracted tier only — the split is contracted versus un-contracted, not bull versus bear.
priorRun.outcome: Vindicated on mechanism: spot and monthly contract turned and buyers called the peak, while the contracted tier firmed into 1Q27.

insights.headline: The bottleneck moved again — from CoWoS to N3, substrates, InP and energised shells
insights.claim: No house argued that GPU supply binds 2027. What binds is converting demand into energised racks: GPUs deliver in weeks, energised megawatts take years.
insights.evidence: JPM puts the CoWoS supply gap at only ~10%, with OSATs supplying 58% of the 2028 increment. N3 runs at 106–113% utilisation with cloud AI taking 73% of 2027 N3 wafers; TSMC raises wafer prices 3–6% from January (grade c). InP: Sumitomo and AXT control ~85% of supply, contract prices +50–60%, no meaningful 6-inch relief before 2028. UBS's delay tracker shows 7.0GW of US capacity affected; chip supply implies ~51GW of 2027 AI additions against 30–50GW a year of deployable powered shell.

priorRun.predicted: The bottleneck migrated past ABF — upstream enablers (TSMC, optics, lasers) hold the margin pool.
priorRun.outcome: Confirmed and extended: CoWoS loosened, N3 and substrates took over, and #20's bull trigger fired as InP tightness persisted through expansion.

insights.headline: The CPU renaissance became a contract — and the contract is really about memory
insights.claim: Agentic AI broadens hardware beyond GPUs, and the first frontier-lab CPU contract shows where the dollars actually go.
insights.evidence: Akamai–Anthropic: $11.6bn over seven years, entirely CPU, with a ~$9bn option, ~$5.5bn of capex and ~95–105MW (8-K, grade a); AKAM rose 19.7%. Jabil holds ~$1.7bn of Akamai memory on consignment, more than the ~$1.0–1.4bn of CPU spend. Mercury: 2Q26 server CPU units +27% y/y, ASPs +44%; Intel 54% unit share (−1,005bp), AMD 28% (+445bp), Arm 18% (+560bp). Every OEM's agentic tier runs on NVIDIA Vera, so the x86 super-cycle may accrue partly to NVIDIA/TSMC.

priorRun.predicted: Not tracked as a contract — server CPU / agentic (#24) was a demand thesis without a named frontier-lab buyer.
priorRun.outcome: #24's bull trigger fired on the Akamai 8-K.

insights.headline: AI entered the Fed's reaction function by name
insights.claim: The rates shock and the credit discrimination are one process: hyperscaler capex adds to inflation, which keeps the Fed hiking and term premium high, which raises the funding cost of the same capex.
insights.evidence: Warsh attributed higher long yields partly to “competition for capital from hyperscaler debt issuance”; Barr listed the AI investment surge alongside tariffs and wars as a reason for more tightening; Guha notes bank C&I loan growth up 230bp since April, plausibly on AI and data-center financing. Markets price ~95bp of hikes through October 2027 (UBS). Warsh's benchmark of private-sector financial conditions puts the terminal rate partly in the hands of the AI trade itself.

priorRun.predicted: ISI's three-wave model counted the AI wave as memory-chip costs, about 2pp of the diffusion index — an input to inflation, not yet a named policy variable.
priorRun.outcome: Escalated to record: both the Chair and a Governor now name AI financing and investment in the reaction function.

insights.headline: Texas dented the behind-the-meter exemption
insights.claim: State restriction is no longer cleanly bullish for on-site power: onsite generation still needs state environmental permits, and Jupiter's air permit is the template.
insights.evidence: Texas halted state data-center permits pending the ERCOT interconnection and water audits (update due 19 October), with >470GW of large loads in the ERCOT queue, and will ask the Legislature to remove data-center incentives. ISI concedes “onsite generation… does not eliminate state environmental permitting.” Oracle's 2.45GW Bloom-powered Jupiter microgrid had its gas route rejected twice before force majeure. ERCOT 2027 forwards round-tripped to ~$38–39/MWh while PJM 2028 makes new highs.

priorRun.predicted: State restriction is bullish behind-the-meter — on-site generation insulates projects from grid politics.
priorRun.outcome: Dented: the permit halt reaches onsite generation too, and #31's bear trigger fired.

agreement.claim: Demand is not the constraint; deliverability and financing are.
agreement.detail: All seven houses, in their own words: UBS “power, permits and financing”, ISI “timing, not demand”, NSR “supply rather than demand”, MS a 33GW net power shortfall for 2026–28, JPM “system delivery and capital return”, Red-Ring “the deliverable system”, TMTB “GPUs deliver in weeks, energised MW take years.”

agreement.detail: Memory, N3 wafers, substrates, InP, turbines and permits are. No house argued that GPU supply binds 2027.

agreement.claim: Compute pricing is rising at the margin.
agreement.detail: CoreWeave +25%, Nebius, Oracle renewals +20%, H100 spot +20–40%, Ornn B200 +50%. No house found GPU rental pricing under pressure this run; ISI states it explicitly.

agreement.claim: The contracted memory tier is tight into 2027.

scenarios.name: Base case
scenarios.body: Choppy, rates-led range; dispersion rather than direction. The NDX holds within ~5–8% of its 22 September high (30,771) while the 10-year stays at 5.0–5.3%. Two rotations continue under the index — contracted over spot (allocated memory, N3 and optics over the commodity channel and PC/phone OEMs) and billing nodes over intermediaries. Credit keeps widening at the borrower tier without contaminating the guarantor tier.

scenarios.name: Bull case
scenarios.body: A relief rally led by long yields. The 10-year falls back toward ~4.80%, the level that forces short-covering with bond CTAs 100% short at the 1st percentile. Because the stock–bond correlation is +28–60%, a bond rally now works as a second long on AI equities, not a hedge.

scenarios.name: Bear case
scenarios.body: The rates shock meets a crowded tape, and the borrower tier cracks. The 10-year pushes toward 5.4–5.5% on a hot ISM, payrolls or an oil spike; the Fed hikes on 28 October. With HF leverage at the 100th percentile and QQQ put/call at the 10th, the drawdown resembles Emanuel's macro-correction set (average −12.9%, 2018 Q4 analogue −20%). The first place it shows is credit, not equity.

bearCase.headline: The financing channel breaks before demand does.
bearCase.body: The Fed keeps hiking into 2027 on AI-driven inflation — the Barr and Warsh reaction function taken literally — and long yields reach 5.5–6%. Four things then fail in sequence. The first place it shows is credit, not equity: CRWV CDS through 1,000bp, a second hyperscale-campus markdown after Jupiter, or a failed or sharply repriced AI-infra deal.

variants.title: 1 · The borrower tier cannot refinance
variants.body: CRWV's ~$102bn 2027–30 funding gap (UBS) meets the $119bn private-credit tech wall of 2028–29 (UBS credit), and a neocloud or campus SPV defaults or restructures.

variants.title: 2 · Guarantor exposure becomes the story
variants.body: NVIDIA's ~$170bn of contingent exposure (MS) and Google's lease guarantees (NSR) move from footnote to headline, and NVDA credit and equity re-price together.

variants.title: 3 · Frontier-lab funding stalls
variants.body: The Anthropic IPO slips into a stressed 2027, which Emanuel says could catalyse “hyperscaler issuance woes”; OpenAI's runway is shorter than the $122bn raise implies.

variants.title: 4 · The un-contracted memory tier rolls into the contracted tier
variants.body: 2027 recontracting happens at lower prices, CXMT's G5 adds ~5% of global bits without a new wafer, and the Lipacis correction plays out (historical average −38% over 13 months).

variants.title: And what would kill the recommendation
variants.body: Drop the underweight and go long the borrower tier outright only if all three happen: CRWV CDS falls back below ~550bp, the Anthropic IPO prices before year-end, and CY27 recontracting clears at a premium to installed rates. Each alone is noise; together they mean the capital markets have decided to underwrite the borrower tier and credit is no longer the binding constraint.
